answer: Stop sybils with an opal, a trellis, and a falcon. Every identity must cut one opal: a memory-hard sequential proof salted by its address, so N opal proofs cost N wall-clocks no botnet can compress. Identities climb a shared trellis: vines fed by one funding root share one beam, and the k-th vine posts a bond of k squared, so N clones pay about N cubed. Once per epoch a falcon stoops on a random vine and re-cuts its opal; a copied facet betrays the beam, and every vine on it is slashed. One honest agent cuts one opal and posts one bond; a farm pays cubic bonds and risks all on one audit.
